content.value_statement: Turkish software teams need consistent documentation, comments, commit messages, and terminology. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code produce clear Turkish developer text.
actual_capabilities: Creates Turkish comment guidance for Python, TypeScript, and Go examples.
Suggests Turkish variable, function, and domain naming conventions.
Formats commit messages with Turkish type labels and concise summaries.
Drafts README sections for setup, quick start, configuration, contribution, and license details.
Provides Turkish equivalents for common software, API, DevOps, security, and data terms.
limitations: Does not validate code correctness or run tests.
Does not translate every framework term when English is the common standard.
Requires project context to choose consistent naming and tone.
Contains documentation examples, not executable automation.

use_cases.title: Document Backend Logic
use_cases.description: Write Turkish comments and error messages that explain business rules without repeating obvious code.

use_cases.title: Prepare Project README Text
use_cases.description: Create Turkish README sections for setup, quick start, features, configuration, contribution, and license notes.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Language
use_cases.description: Align commit labels, domain terms, log messages, and naming choices across a Turkish software team.

prompt_templates.title: Add Turkish Comments
prompt_templates.prompt: Add Turkish comments to this function. Explain why important decisions exist, and avoid comments that repeat obvious code.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Turkish Commit Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Write a Turkish commit message for this change. Use the project type labels and keep the subject under 72 characters.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Turkish README Section
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft Turkish README sections for installation, quick start, configuration, contribution, and license. Keep the text direct and practical.

prompt_templates.title: Standardize Project Terminology
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request for team-wide language rules.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review these names, messages, and docs for Turkish terminology consistency. Recommend which terms should remain English and explain why.

output_examples.input: A developer asks for Turkish comments on session validation logic.
output: The response explains the reason for validation and permission checks.
It avoids comments that only restate each operation.
It keeps framework terms understandable for the team.

output_examples.input: A maintainer needs a Turkish commit message for moving invoice logic into a service layer.
output_examples.output: The response provides a short Turkish subject and an optional body explaining the architectural reason.

output_examples.input: A team wants Turkish technical terms for API and security documentation.
output_examples.output: The response suggests consistent Turkish equivalents and notes terms that are commonly kept in English.

best_practices: Use Turkish for domain concepts and keep established framework terms in English when teams expect them.
Explain why code exists, not only what each line does.
Keep commit subject lines short and add context in the body when needed.
anti_patterns: Mixing Turkish and English names without a project rule.
Translating framework keywords in ways that confuse developers.
Writing comments that repeat obvious code behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill write production code?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on Turkish documentation, comments, commit messages, naming guidance, and terminology.

faq.question: Can it help with README files?
faq.answer: Yes. It provides a Turkish README structure for setup, quick start, features, configuration, contribution, and license sections.

faq.question: Should every technical term be translated?
faq.answer: No. The skill recommends keeping common framework and library terms in English when that improves clarity.

faq.question: Can it enforce a team naming standard?
faq.answer: It can suggest consistent rules, but the team must approve and apply the standard in the codebase.

faq.question: Does it run shell commands?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains documentation examples only and does not define executable automation.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It is listed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
